metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Australia

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Australia using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, stratified, clustered sample intended to represent 15-year-old students in participating countries/economies; analyses in the PISA database are therefore typically conducted with sampling weights to account for unequal selection probabilities and clustering at school level. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name or whether replicate weights were used, so the precise implementation details are not recoverable from the provided text. For interpretation, the reported uncertainty (e.g., 95% confidence intervals) indicates that the OECD’s standard PISA variance estimation approach was applied, but the specific weight/replication settings are not documented in this excerpt.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive results factsheet rather than an empirical student-level modeling paper that specifies how plausible values (PVs) were generated/combined for a predictive target. The outcomes reported are PISA creative thinking proficiency scores and related proficiency-level shares, which are produced within the PISA scaling framework, but the excerpt does not provide the PV combination rule or missing-data procedure used in the scaling. Therefore, PV handling and missing-data handling are not reported at the level required for replication from this factsheet text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample for the Australia factsheet consists of 13,437 students in 743 schools who completed the PISA 2022 assessment in mathematics, reading, or science and are included in the creative thinking reporting for Australia. The excerpt does not describe additional exclusions beyond the standard PISA participation and completion requirements for the creative thinking volume; it also notes that PISA 2022 was implemented in 81 countries/economies and that some countries/economies may have sampling-standard issues (asterisks), but Australia is presented without such a caution marker in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes Australia’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking test for 15-year-old students. The creative thinking assessment includes 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. Australia’s mean creative thinking score is 37 (out of 60), significantly above the OECD average of 33. The factsheet also reports proficiency distributions (88% at least Level 3; 43% at Level 5 or 6) and relative strengths by ideation process and domain context, with higher relative performance for generating creative ideas and for written/visual expression. It further documents within-country gaps by socioeconomic status and gender, and associations between creative thinking and students’ beliefs/attitudes and school environment indicators, while noting that some countries/economies may have sampling-standard limitations due to COVID-19.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is for an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet (descriptive reporting) rather than an empirical ML study that trains and evaluates predictive models. As a result, there is no student-level ML pipeline, no explicit PV-combination rule, and no missing-data handling procedure described in the provided text. The factsheet’s purpose is to communicate benchmarked performance and subgroup patterns using PISA’s established scaling and reporting framework, so ML-specific fields are intentionally left empty.
